structure.heading: Sourcing Strategy: Make-versus-Buy, Preferred Supplier Selection, and Contracting Approach
text_content: **Sourcing Strategy: Make-versus-Buy, Preferred Supplier Selection, and Contracting Approach**

The make‑versus‑buy recommendation will be finalized on 2026-02-15 following a TCO, risk, and capability assessment across on‑premise and cloud alternatives. The analysis prioritizes scalability, operational maturity, and compliance posture; vendor-managed cloud services are recommended for core compute and networking where unit economics and time-to-market improvements exceed in-house investment thresholds. Governance includes CFO and CIO sign-off and a transition plan with 90-day implementation sprints.

service levels (15%). Evaluation included reference checks, financial stability reviews, and proof-of-concept outcomes to validate integration and performance expectations. Contract awards will be staged by region and workload.

Contracts will emphasize measurable SLAs, commercial incentives, service credits, and exit rights, with quarterly KPIs and a central vendor governance board. Target contracted savings is 8.5% ($4.4M) by 2026-12-31. Payment terms, audit rights, and renewal options will be standardized to mitigate risk and enable reporting against savings milestones effectively periodically.

structure.heading: FY2026 Category Spend Baseline and Demand Forecast for Data Center & Cloud Infrastructure
text_content: **FY2026 Category Spend Baseline and Demand Forecast for Data Center & Cloud Infrastructure**

FY2025 established the baseline for Data Center & Cloud Infrastructure spend at $48.6M, reflecting contract cycles and migration activities completed during the 2024–2025 fiscal period. The top three subcategories in FY2025 were Public Cloud ($18.2M), Data Center Colocation ($12.4M), and Network Connectivity ($7.9M), together accounting for 78% of total category spend. Other material line items included hardware refresh, managed services, and professional services. Monthly and quarterly invoicing patterns show peak consumption in Q3 and Q4 driven by year-end project acceleration. This baseline underpins the FY2026 planning process and provides a factual foundation for capacity, budget cadence, and supplier engagement timelines. It will inform prioritization and contingency.

The FY2026 forecasted category spend is $52.0M, representing a 7.0% increase versus FY2025 and reflecting a planned 15% compute growth predominantly executed within public cloud environments (AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud Platform). Forecast drivers include higher on‑demand and reserved-instance consumption, increased egress and data transfer charges, and additional colocation rack space to support hybrid architectures. Modeling assumptions for the FY2026 plan include: 1. Compute growth realized as a mix of 70% public cloud and 30% colocation; 2. a 6% average pricing inflation across network services; and 3. a 12‑month contract renewal cycle for major suppliers. These assumptions are subject to quarterly review and reforecasting and governance.

Operationalizing the FY2026 forecast requires subcategory phasing, KPIs, and contingency triggers to translate the planned 15% compute growth into capacity and budget actions. Recommended phasing is weighted to project timelines: Q1 20%, Q2 25%, Q3 30%, and Q4 25% of incremental spend, aligning with procurement and implementation milestones. Key metrics to track monthly include: - cost per vCPU-hour or equivalent; - network egress ($ per TB); - colocation rack utilization (%). Set control thresholds with automatic review when monthly variance exceeds 5% or when cumulative spend versus forecast deviates by $0.5M. Maintain a 3% contingency reserve and quarterly reforecast cadence. Monthly reports delivered to finance, IT, procurement.
